finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is interpolated into the SQL string through an f-string. An attacker can break out of the LIKE literal and run arbitrary SELECT logic, for example a UNION to read other tables or columns.

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') takes the raw query string value
term is formatted directly into the SQL text and executed
The rows are returned as JSON, so the injected query's results go back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No parameterization, escaping, allowlist or authentication on the path. The other two queries (app.py:18, app.py:25) use ? placeholders, so this one is the only injectable query. sqlite3 execute() rejects multiple statements, which rules out stacked queries, but UNION-based data extraction still works.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 reads q raw and app.py:12 f-string-interpolates it into the LIKE literal with no parameterization, auth or allowlist, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so a UNION SELECT (two columns, e.g. from sqlite_master) is exploitable by an anonymous user; the queries at app.py:18 and :25 use ? placeholders as claimed.
